jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation
jobs.location: US, CA, Santa Clara US, TX, Remote US, PA, Remote US, WA, Remote US, CA, Remote US, MA, Remote
jobs.jd: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world. We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups: Internal partners , including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators. Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages. The research community , through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues. The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward. What you'll be doing: Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API. Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row. Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results. Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap. Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists. Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences. What we need to see: BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries. Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on. Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost. Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools. Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library. RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL. Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses. Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding. Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, and you want to build the open-source infrastructure behind trustworthy user simulation, we want to hear from you! Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are: 187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits . Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 29, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Product Owner für Agentic-Twin-Plattform explore (m/w/d)
jobs.jd: Pfaffenhofen a. d. Ilm • Vollzeit • ab sofort Wir sind EXP Software GmbH: Wir sind ein Team aus rund 25 Softwareentwickler*innen mit Herz, Humor und Leidenschaft für Technologie. Wir bauen explore, eine Agentic-Twin-Plattform, die Unternehmen dabei hilft, komplexe Prozesse durch autonome KI-Agenten abzubilden und zu automatisieren.Unser Produkt wächst und damit auch die Anforderungen an jemanden, der den Überblick behält: zwischen dem, was Kunden brauchen, was die Geschäftsführung vorhat, und dem, was das Entwicklungsteam realistisch umsetzen kann. Genau diese Brücke baust du. Wir suchen keinen Prozess-Verwalter, der Tickets schiebt. Wir suchen jemanden, der explore wirklich versteht, sich für das Produkt begeistert und mit Klarheit und Konsequenz dafür sorgt, dass die richtigen Dinge in der richtigen Reihenfolge gebaut werden. Aufgaben Produktvision & Roadmap Du erstellst und verantwortest das Product Backlog für explore: Pflege, Priorisierung und kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung in enger Abstimmung mit Geschäftsführung, Kunden und Entwicklungsteam. Du übersetzt Geschäftsziele und Kundenanforderungen in klare, umsetzbare User Stories und Akzeptanzkriterien, und das präzise genug für das Team und verständlich genug für alle anderen. Du setzt klare Prioritäten und begründest sie: Was bauen wir als nächstes – und warum? Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung eine mittelfristige Produkt-Roadmap und hältst sie am Leben. Du durchdringst die explore-Plattform inhaltlich: Agentenlogik, Automatisierungskonzepte, Möglichkeiten und Grenzen und bringst Impulse aus dem KI-Markt direkt ins Produkt. Team & Wissenstransfer Du führst regelmäßige Gespräche mit Bestandskunden, verstehst ihre Arbeitsprozesse und erkennst, welche Anforderungen wirklich wichtig sind und welche nur laut. Du übersetzt Kundenfeedback, Support-Erkenntnisse und Marktbeobachtungen in konkrete Produktentscheidungen. Du bist die zentrale Anlaufstelle für eingehende Anforderungen und sorgst dafür, dass nichts verloren geht, alles bewertet wird und Entscheidungen nachvollziehbar sind. Du nutzt KI-Tools selbstverständlich in deiner eigenen Arbeit: zur Recherche, Dokumentation, Analyse, Priorisierung und Automatisierung. Zusammenarbeit & Steuerung Du arbeitest täglich eng mit unseren Entwicklerinnen und Entwicklern zusammen: Sprint Planning, Refinements, Reviews; du bist dabei und bringst dich inhaltlich ein. Du beantwortest Rückfragen des Teams schnell und verbindlich, nimmst Ergebnisse ab und stellst sicher, dass sie den definierten Akzeptanzkriterien entsprechen. Du verstehst technische Zusammenhänge gut genug, um sinnvolle Abwägungen zwischen Aufwand und Nutzen zu treffen. Du planst Demos vor Kunden und Stakeholdern und führst diese direkt im Produkt auch selbst aus. Qualifikation Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Owner oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle im Software- oder Tech-Umfeld und weißt, wie agile Produktentwicklung in der Praxis funktioniert. Eine Zertifizierung als Product Owner ist wünschenswert, aber kein Muss. Du hast ein solides Verständnis von Softwareentwicklung und KI-Konzepten. Ein Informatikstudium oder eine Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker ist wünschenswert, aber nicht zwingend. Entscheidend ist, dass du mit dem Entwicklungsteam auf Augenhöhe kommunizieren kannst. Du verstehst, wie LLMs, Agenten und Automatisierungssysteme funktionieren; nicht zwingend auf Code-Ebene, aber konzeptionell sicher genug, um Produktentscheidungen darauf zu gründen. Du kannst gut zuhören, präzise zusammenfassen und Anforderungen so formulieren, dass sie das Team direkt umsetzen kann. Du arbeitest strukturiert, priorisierst klar und verlierst auch bei vielen parallelen Themen nicht den Überblick. Du kommunizierst sicher auf allen Ebenen: mit Kunden, Entwicklern und der Geschäftsführung gleichermaßen und verwendest jeweils die richtige Ansprache. Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sind Voraussetzung; Englisch ist im technischen Kontext selbstverständlich. Wir wünschen uns jemanden, der hauptsächlich bei uns vor Ort ist. Mindestens 3 von 5 Tagen in unserem Büro in Pfaffenhofen. Remote-Tage sind selbstverständlich möglich und Teil unserer Arbeitsweise. Benefits Ein unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag mit 30 Tagen Urlaub. Flexibles Arbeiten und familienfreundliche Arbeitszeitgestaltung. Ein kollegiales, wertschätzendes Arbeitsumfeld mit viel Raum für eigene Ideen. Budget für Weiterbildung und die Tools, die du brauchst. Du gestaltest aktiv mit, wohin sich explore entwickelt - mit echtem Einfluss auf Produktvision und Roadmap. Du arbeitest an einer Plattform am Puls der aktuellen KI-Entwicklung und hast damit Einfluss auf Architektur und Produktrichtung. Klingt nach dir? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung. Schick uns: Deinen Lebenslauf. Optional: Nachweis deiner PO-Zertifizierung. Optional: Ein kurzes Beispiel, wie du eine komplexe Kundenanforderung in konkrete User Stories übersetzt hast. Das interessiert uns mehr als ein klassisches Anschreiben. Fragen? Wir melden uns schnell. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

We work at the intersection of partner engineering, NVIDIA’s AI platform, and product development. You will lead sophisticated technical projects from initial exploration through architecture, prototyping, performance optimization, production rollout, and field enablement. Together, we will help partners adopt NVIDIA technologies and GPU-accelerated infrastructure to bring next-generation AI products to market. What you'll be doing: Lead technical delivery for strategic Agentic AI partner engagements from discovery and architecture through PoC, production readiness, rollout, and scale. Design and build enterprise-grade agentic systems, including multi-agent workflows, tool-using agents, RAG-integrated applications, planning, memory, evaluation, and guardrail patterns. Lead deep architecture reviews with partner engineering teams, driving tradeoffs across model quality, latency, efficiency, cost, retrieval quality, reliability, safety, security, and observability. Build hands-on PoCs, benchmarks, reference architectures, and reusable blueprints that help Enterprise ISVs and NVIDIA field teams move from exploration to production. Guide partners on model customization and post-training workflows, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning methods, human or AI feedback, direct preference optimization, PEFT/LoRA, synthetic data generation, evaluation, and regression analysis. Work with agent harnesses and execution environments such as OpenShell, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, LangChain, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, or similar frameworks. jobs.jd: ⌘Role Overview The Data Scientist is the first hire on the team whose job is to put machine learning into production , not just into a notebook. Production ML Development Build, validate, and ship ML models (propensity, pricing/discount optimization, personalization, churn/LTV) that go live in the product, not just proof-of-concept notebooks. Personalization across the journey: from paywall to lifecycle Design and ship the personalized discounting model: who gets what offer, and why, served at the moment of the paywall decision. Build the measurement framework so pricing/discount decisions are defensible to finance and leadership. 3. ML Infrastructure & MLOps (GCP) Stand up our first low-latency model serving pattern on GCP (e.g., Vertex AI endpoints, Cloud Run, or equivalent) Define the feature pipeline pattern: what's precomputed in BigQuery/dbt vs. what needs to be fresh/real-time via Pub/Sub or similar. Set up model monitoring: drift, staleness, prediction quality so a live model doesn't silently degrade. 4. Product & Engineering Partnership Sit close to Product and Engineering, not just Data this role is measured by what ships to actual users, not just notebooks Translate a product problem ("how might we reactive lapsed payers") into a modeling problem, and a model output into an API contract Engineering can build against. Document handoffs clearly enough that Engineering can own the serving layer long-term without you as a bottleneck. 5. Experimentation & Causal Inference Design uplift/causal models where "who responds to a discount" matters more than "who churns" . Run and interpret experiments that isolate the model's actual incremental impact on revenue/retention. Design the experimentation program for improving data science and machine learning models with the same rigour we use across our already ongoing experimentation programs ⌘Expected Outcomes Personalized discounting model live in production , serving real paywall decisions to real users: shipped end-to-end, not a prototype sitting in staging. A documented, reusable low-latency serving pattern established on GCP (Vertex AI endpoints or Cloud Run) — the next model doesn't require rebuilding this from scratch. Proven incremental lift on a core business metric (paywall conversion, discount margin efficiency, or lapsed-payer reactivation — pick the one you want as the flagship KPI), demonstrated through a controlled experiment, not just before/after comparison. Model monitoring in place — drift and staleness alerts mean the team knows within days, not months, if a live model silently degrades. A repeatable model-to-production playbook that others in the team can follow ⌘Skills & Competencies Must have (hard skills) Strong Python for data science and ML (scikit-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM; PyTorch or TensorFlow a plus if deep learning is relevant to future use cases). Proven track record shipping models to production, not just modeling in a notebook. Can talk through at least one model that served live traffic. Hands-on experience with a cloud ML platform, ideally GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery ML, Cloud Run/Functions) or fast ability to translate equivalent AWS/Azure experience. Solid SQL; comfortable working against a dbt/BigQuery warehouse. Software engineering fundamentals: git, code review, testing, CI/CD: You'll be shipping code Engineering has to trust. Causal inference / uplift modelling or applied experimentation experience: pricing and discounting need "what if we hadn't," not just "who churns." Nice to have Experience with streaming/event pipelines (Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Kafka): useful as we move off pure batch. Experience with pricing, discounting, personalization specifically. Familiarity with feature stores or the DIY equivalent (versioned feature pipelines). Multi-armed bandits or reinforcement learning for pricing/personalization. Startup experience: comfortable being the first person to build something rather than joining an existing ML platform team. Soft skills Genuinely energised by "does this move the metric," not just "is this model accurate." Can hold their own in a room with Engineering and with Business: Speaks commercial as well as the language of engineering Explains modeling tradeoffs in plain business terms to Product/leadership without dumbing it down or using too much jargon Comfortable owning ambiguity — this role is defining the pattern, not following one. ⌘ Required experience 4–7 years in a data scientist / ML engineer role, with at least one model you personally took from prototype to live production serving real users or real traffic. jobs.jd: Build the Path Forward At Path Robotics , we’re building the future of embodied intelligence. Our AI-driven systems enable robots to adapt, learn, and perform in the real world closing the skilled labor gap and transforming industries. We go beyond traditional methods, combining perception, reasoning, and control to deliver field-ready AI that is risk-aware, reliable, and continuously improving through real-world use. Big, hard problems are our everyday work, and our team of intelligent, humble, and driven people make the impossible possible together. We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Robotics team. You'll use machine learning to improve how our robots plan, scan, and act. You'll frame real robot problems as well-defined ML problems, train models on data that a fleet of production robotic cells generates every day, and ship them into a production stack where they work alongside classical planning and perception. Your models run on live robots doing real work for customers. What You'll Do Frame open-ended problems in planning, scanning, and robot behavior as well-defined ML problems. Train models that work with classical methods, such as initial guesses and learned costs for trajectory optimization, plan quality and feasibility predictors, and learned collision models. Develop viewpoint planning policies that choose where and how to scan, and predict scan quality before the robot commits. Apply imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and generative models such as diffusion and flow matching where they outperform classical baselines. Build production ML pipelines: datasets from fleet logs and simulation, training, and metrics. Evaluate models in the loop, with offline metrics that predict gains on the robot, failure-mode analysis, and calibrated confidence that determines when the system falls back to classical methods. Own your models end to end, from prototype to deployment on live robotic cells, with low-latency inference and monitoring. Who You Are An MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field. 4+ years of applied machine learning for robotics or autonomy, in research or industry. Fluent in Python with PyTorch or JAX, and experienced training, evaluating, and deploying deep learning models. Strong foundations in linear algebra, 3D geometry, kinematics, and optimization. You've run your methods on real robot hardware. You explain model results and their limits clearly, so planning, perception, and field teams know when to trust them. Preferred C++, and experience deploying models into a C++ or ROS 2 production stack. Motion planning, trajectory optimization, or collision checking. Active perception, next-best-view or informative path planning, or 3D point cloud learning. Uncertainty estimation and calibration, or Bayesian and information-theoretic planning. GPU inference optimization (CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX). Simulation and sim-to-real transfer (Isaac Lab, MuJoCo). Publications at RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or similar venues. jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer – Models in Production (m/f/d)
jobs.jd: Anyone can train a model in a notebook these days. Getting it into production, keeping it accurate month after month and turning its output into decisions people actually make is a different story. That's the job. For a renowned automotive manufacturer in Munich, we are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer who builds models that matter for a premium brand. You work with structured and unstructured data, take models all the way into production and make sure they keep delivering. Your results shape strategic decisions and the experience of customers who expect nothing less than premium. What makes this role different You don't build models that end up in a slide deck. You own them end to end, from the raw data to the deployed model to the insight a decision maker acts on. One client, one location, one team in Munich, with direct access to the people who use your work. And you are the person who brings machine learning into the business. You explain what a model can and cannot do, teach colleagues how to use it and help them ask better questions of their data. Degree or not, what counts is what you have built. If you have a proven track record of shipping machine learning applications, for example in open source, that is as valuable to us as a degree. The goal is ambitious. Move machine learning out of experiments and into the decisions a premium brand makes every day, from strategy to the experience of its customers. What you will do Develop and implement machine learning models for premium automotive applications Collect, clean and prepare structured and unstructured data so your models are built on something solid Deploy models to production, monitor them and keep them performing over time Turn results into clear insights that support strategic decisions and enhance the customer experience Document your work and teach others how machine learning and AI can be used in their daily business What you bring A degree in a technical field with a strong focus on machine learning, or a proven track record of building machine learning applications, for example in open source projects Outstanding Python skills and a real appreciation for clean, well documented code Experience developing and running applications in the cloud Hands-on experience taking models into production and monitoring them, ideally with MLOps tools A genuine passion for machine learning and AI and their potential in real business applications The ability to explain a complex topic to a manager in the morning and dig into a data pipeline in the afternoon Fluent English; German is a plus, but not a must You'll stand out if you have shipped models that are used in day-to-day business, maintained or contributed to open source machine learning projects, or worked with automotive or industrial data. jobs.jd:
Growth at CFO Insights

Are you looking master the latest AI tools, build agents, and put them to work on real business problems? Are you the person who gets things done and gets their hands dirty? If so, now is the time to apply for the AI Implementation role at Private Equity Insights.

You will join an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people working on one mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why CFO Insights

CFO Insights is Northern Europe’s largest CFO forum and aims to connect and develop CFOs, finance leaders, and tomorrow's innovators by addressing the issues of the future CFO. We are connecting more than 11,000 professionals from more than 15 countries.

CFO Insights is part of United Media which focuses on building large scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, HR, private equity, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Unlimted AI Tokens We are ready to invest in AI and will equip you with all the tools and accesses you need to create 1000x results
  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. AI mastery, fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Implement AI that deliver real impact Identify where AI can do more and better impact than a human ever could. Measure the time saved and commercial impact
  • Master AI and automation. Build reliable AI agents and connected workflows for client delivery, market research, meeting intelligence, business development, and revenue acceleration..
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

jobs.title: Sr Applied Scientist, Embedded Battery Algorithms, Energy Storage
jobs.jd: Do you want to write the algorithms that control next-generation batteries, and shape the future of energy storage? This role sits where electrochemistry, data/ML, and control theory meet. You will develop the physics-informed and data-driven methods that estimate state of charge, health, power capability, and remaining life, and validate them against lab and fleet data until they are ready to ship. Your algorithms will decide how hard a battery can be pushed, when it needs attention, and how long it will last, so they shape the safety, warranty, and economics of the whole product. You will work side by side with cell, systems, and software engineers, and as an early hire you will help define how we develop and validate battery algorithms. This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic and international travel, up to 10% of the time. Key job responsibilities - Develop and own algorithms for state of charge, state of health, power capability, and remaining useful life, combining physics-based models with data-driven and estimation methods. - Deliver validated reference implementations, test vectors, and accuracy targets that define what production code must achieve. - Design the test plans and data needed to develop and validate algorithms, working with the cell and testing teams to turn lab and field data into model improvements. - Analyze algorithm performance across the deployed fleet, find where models drift or fail, and drive improvements. - Own the accuracy and robustness of battery algorithms, and sign off that production implementations match the validated reference. Provide algorithm evidence for safety certification. A day in the life Your week moves between data, models, and experiments. One day you might be working out why a health estimate drifts on cells that have aged in the field, and the next deciding which model structure holds accuracy at cold temperatures. You could be designing a test with the cell team to expose a behavior your model misses, or reviewing an implementation with an applied scientist to confirm that what ships matches what you validated. You will regularly share results with software, systems, and cell leaders, and your findings will shape decisions well beyond the algorithm itself. About the team We are building Amazon's energy storage capability, providing power for advanced technologies while contributing to a stable grid. Our product is highly connected, yet secure and resilient by design. We own it end to end, from software, ML, and controls through system design to cell selection and supply, and on to a safety-certified product in the field. The organization operates like a startup inside Amazon: small, fast-moving, and accountable for our decisions. We work across hardware, software, and science, with suppliers and partners worldwide, and with Amazon infrastructure, procurement, legal, and finance. The organization is at an early stage and growing quickly. You will be among the first algorithm hires, so you will help shape how we design, build, certify, and ship, with a direct line of sight to the product and business decisions your work informs. This is a dynamic role that will regularly present new challenges as the product and organization evolve. - Master's degree in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - 8+ years of experience developing battery algorithms or battery models in industry or research with a Master's degree, or 5+ years with a PhD. - Extensive experience launching battery products with leading automotive or grid storage OEMs may be considered in place of some of this experience. - Experience developing state of charge or state of health estimation algorithms for lithium-ion batteries, including building equivalent circuit models and using methods such as Kalman filtering or data-driven models. - Experience validating battery algorithms against laboratory and field data. - Expert proficiency in Python for building and validating battery models, and the ability to prototype algorithms in C. - Familiarity with automotive or battery energy storage system (BESS) safety standards, such as ISO 26262, UL 1973, or UL 9540A. - PhD in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - Experience building physics-based electrochemical models, such as the Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN) or single particle model (SPM) or other advanced battery models, and with lithium-ion aging mechanisms. - Experience with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, including state of charge estimation across the flat voltage plateau and hysteresis. - Familiarity with lithium-ion failure modes and abuse hazards, such as overcharge, internal short, and thermal runaway, and experience developing algorithms to detect them. - Experience designing battery test protocols, such as hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC), drive or duty cycles, and impedance spectroscopy. - Experience making technical trade-offs on a safety-critical product, where certification and field reliability constrain cost and schedule. - Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, and effective across cultures, companies, and time zones.
